title: Cayley–Hamilton Linear Recurrence of Pell Solutions
problemStatement: The root pell-equation entry classifies solutions of x² − Dy² = 1 multiplicatively (powers of the fundamental solution in ℤ[√D]). Does this force an additive second-order linear recurrence on the coordinate sequences, and is its coefficient determined by the generator alone — explaining the D = 2 coefficient 6 of pell-equation-oq-06-oq-03?
currentState: COMPLETED, 0-axiom verified (no native_decide). Shipped as gallery entry pell-equation-oq-07 (PR #27637).
knownResults: Pell coordinate sequences are Lucas-type sequences with characteristic polynomial t² − (2x₁)t + 1 (classical).
Mathlib's Pell.Solution₁ records the multiplicative/group structure but not the coordinate recurrence.

insights: Every a ∈ ℤ[√d] satisfies its own characteristic relation a² = (2·re a)·a − N(a) with NO hypothesis: trace = 2·re a = a + ā, determinant = N(a) = a·ā. This single Cayley–Hamilton fact drives the whole recurrence.
Multiplying the characteristic relation by aⁿ propagates it to the power sequence (aⁿ⁺² = (2·re a)·aⁿ⁺¹ − N(a)·aⁿ); both ℤ-linear coordinate functionals re, im inherit the SAME recurrence.

For a Pell solution N(a) = 1 the recurrence collapses to uₙ₊₂ = (2·x₁)·uₙ₊₁ − uₙ — the coefficient is twice the first coordinate of the generator, the general-D source of the D = 2 coefficient 6 = 2·re⟨3,2⟩.

Slug discipline: the top-level numbered oq-NN slots of pell-equation map to specific registered open questions (oq-03 = polynomial-time, oq-05 = degree>2 norm equations). A self-generated follow-up must use a FREE slot (oq-07) to avoid mislabeling an unsolved problem as solved.

mathlibGaps: Mathlib has Zsqrtd norm/multiplication and Pell.Solution₁ (group structure) but NO general statement that the coordinate power sequences satisfy the trace recurrence; this entry supplies it for arbitrary d.
nextSteps: Derive Binet/matrix-power closed forms from the recurrence, making the eigenvalue picture (roots of t² − 2x₁t + 1 = conjugate units) explicit.
Prove a general-D Cassini/Catalan identity xₙ₋₁xₙ₊₁ − xₙ² = const, generalizing the D = 2 determinant identity of pell-equation-oq-06-oq-05.
Connect re_pell_unique to Mathlib's Pell.Solution₁: the coordinate maps of a fundamental generator are the unique solutions of the trace recurrence with standard initial data.
knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETE: general-D Cayley–Hamilton recurrence aⁿ⁺² = (2·re a)·aⁿ⁺¹ − N(a)·aⁿ for ℤ[√d] power sequences; Pell collapse uₙ₊₂ = 2x₁·uₙ₊₁ − uₙ; recovers D=2 coefficient 6. 0-axiom verified.
